details: hijiko-parser@1.0.1 is a near-empty package (index.js is a single console.log line) whose only real function is to make npm fetch a dependency from a raw, plaintext HTTP tarball URL outside the npm registry: dependencies.marker-script-suffix-mapper resolves to hxxp://web[.]vitemaweed[.]fr:4873/marker-script-suffix-mapper/-/marker-script-suffix-mapper-1[.]0[.]18[.]tgz, pinned in package.json and repeated in npm-shrinkwrap.json so the install resolves to that host. Installing it pulls an unauditable, tamperable third-party tarball from port 4873 on web[.]vitemaweed[.]fr (a Verdaccio-style registry impersonating npm's audit trail), and the package also declares a shell-based postinstall hook ("/bin/bash -i -c 'echo installed'"). The dependency runs its own install lifecycle with the installer's privileges.
